content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early periods, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes near the end of the history often trigger a sharp price rebound, indicating sentiment-driven momentum.", "Model forecasts show mean-reversion bias when true outcomes dip below historical averages, suggesting underestimation of volatility.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish, as models avoid over-optimism.", "Lagging forecasts tend to underestimate sharp price increases, particularly in the first 5-7 days of the forecast horizon.", "High sentiment values correlate with higher forecasted prices, but often fail to capture sudden downward corrections.", "Models exhibit significant bias when sentiment is low, leading to underestimation of price drops or volatility spikes.", "Forecast accuracy is highest when the true outcome aligns with the model’s early trend, indicating calibration to recent price behavior."]}
